eligibility.evidence: Abstract and Sec 1-3: six LLMs generate random binary coin-flip sequences, the 'classic behavioral-science paradigm' of human random-sequence production; cites Nickerson & Butler 2009, Bar-Hillel et al. 2014, Rapoport & Budescu 1992 (E2 test a). New model outputs and a behavioural outcome (alternation, runs, heads rate) are analysed against human data from prior work (E1, E3, E4). Preprint, English, 2024+.

A.title: Heads, Tails, and AI Fails: LLMs, Randomness, and Human Judgments

E.headline: LLMs reproduce canonical human randomness biases (over-alternation, long-run aversion, first-flip heads bias) but often amplify them or add model-specific distortions; temperature does not remove them.

G.notes: Group comparisons rest on previously published human numbers (no human sample, no tests on main effects). Alternation values for 4 models rest on Table 25 with temperature unstated. Table 14 and Table 25 disagree for the same model. Qwen is '2' in Table 3 and '2.5' in Table 4. Code/data only 'in supplementary materials', no link.
